title: Correcting Chilton's Who's Who; the Sammy Price audition
summary: Budd sets the record straight that Sammy Price did not organize the Blue Moon Chasers, who auditioned and rejected him.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: All right. Yes, we went back, and of course we were back in school. We worked around, and actually, at that time we had on piano a great little man by the name of Charlie Durham. Charlie Durham was a great fullback on the highschool team. And he played beautiful piano. He had been working with us, and he was a little short guy, could do ten seconds flat, a hundred yards, in his football togs. He was a great little fullback.

And so Charlie had to leave the band, and we were auditioning piano players. So I just want to make one correction in John Chilton's Who's Who of Jazz, and where he mentioned that when I changed to tenor sax and played with local Blue Moon Chasers, and occasionally in a big band organized by

Sammy Price, in 1927, this is really not correct, although I know the dates and things get mixed up, but I would like to set the record straight right here with Milt Hinton. The Blue Moon Chasers, as I had said previously, was organized by our little school band, which had been going since the Moonlight Melody Six, and I said that when we went to high school we changed the name to the Blue Moon Chasers.

Now how Sammy Price came into the picture, it was like this. We were looking for a piano player. So Sammy Price was playing piano at that time, pretty good! And so in -- in this audition he had invited us to his house, and his mother had fixed sandwiches and cold drinks and everything for us while she was away, we did a rehearsal with Sammy Price.

Well, this sounds funny, because Sammy has now become to be a big star, but at that time we figured he was not good enough for our band, and so we drank him up, lemonade and whatnot, ate all his food, rehearsed at his house, and then told him we were very sorry, that we couldn't use him.

But Sammy had nothing to do with organizing the Blue Moon Chasers. I just wanted to set that record straight. I know it was a mistake made there, but I mean that's all right with me. We all make mistakes.
Now, however, Sammy is doing very well, and I'm going
down to see him. He's working at a place called West End, with Joe Jones.
I've got to go down and see them, and have a lot of fun with them.
